transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) err FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1,3

content.content: {"error": "Query execution failed: Invalid Input Error: Required module 'pytz' failed to import, due to the following Python exception:\nModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytz'", "query": "SELECT * FROM abnormal_logs", "available_tables": ["abnormal_logs"]}

content.text: Frontend and search are clearly slow in the incident period. Next I'll break down the spans by name, and check the log query that failed on pytz.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,2) p90, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code!='OK' AND attr_status_code!='UNSET' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) nonok FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,2), sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code!='OK' AND attr_status_code!='UNSET' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The key finding so far: `search` calls `rate.Rate/GetRates` and waits about 1.65 s, but the `rate` server span takes only 0.48 ms. The delay sits between the two services, not inside `rate`. I'll check the network metrics on that connection.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avgv, round(max(value),2) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 2,3,4,5,1

content.content: {"error": "Result exceeds token budget", "estimated_tokens": 15494, "token_limit": 5000, "suggestions": ["Reduce the LIMIT value", "Filter rows with WHERE clauses to reduce result size", "Use aggregation (COUNT, SUM, AVG) instead of retrieving raw rows"]}

input.query: SELECT metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs, count(DISTINCT attr_source) srcs, count(DISTINCT attr_destination) dsts FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: No hubble per-connection metrics in this case. I'll compare per-service key metrics (CPU, memory, JVM, restarts, uptime) between normal and abnormal.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, round(avg(CASE WHEN p='ab' THEN value END),3) ab_avg, round(avg(CASE WHEN p='n' THEN value END),3) n_avg, round(max(CASE WHEN p='ab' THEN value END),3) ab_max, round(max(CASE WHEN p='n' THEN value END),3) n_max FROM (SELECT 'ab' p, * FROM abnormal_metrics UNION ALL SELECT 'n', * FROM normal_metrics) GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.content: {"error": "Result exceeds token budget", "estimated_tokens": 24129, "token_limit": 5000, "suggestions": ["Reduce the LIMIT value", "Filter rows with WHERE clauses to reduce result size", "Use aggregation (COUNT, SUM, AVG) instead of retrieving raw rows"]}

input.query: SELECT metric, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: Now I'll compare CPU and memory per service between the two periods, using aggregates only.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, round(avg(CASE WHEN p='ab' THEN value END),3) ab_avg, round(avg(CASE WHEN p='n' THEN value END),3) n_avg FROM (SELECT 'ab' p, * FROM abnormal_metrics UNION ALL SELECT 'n', * FROM normal_metrics) WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','k8s.pod.cpu.usage') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: No CPU or memory saturation anywhere. Next I'll check restarts, uptime and pod network errors.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, round(avg(CASE WHEN p='ab' THEN value END),2) ab_avg, round(avg(CASE WHEN p='n' THEN value END),2) n_avg, round(max(CASE WHEN p='ab' THEN value END),2) ab_max, round(max(CASE WHEN p='n' THEN value END),2) n_max FROM (SELECT 'ab' p, * FROM abnormal_metrics_sum UNION ALL SELECT 'n', * FROM normal_metrics_sum) WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.errors','k8s.pod.uptime') AND service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation','profile','geo') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: No restarts, no uptime resets and no network errors, so the fault is not a pod loss or a resource squeeze. I'll look at individual search→rate call pairs to see how the extra time is distributed, and where it lands.

input.query: SELECT c.trace_id, c.service_name csvc, c.attr_k8s_pod_name cpod, round(c.duration/1e6,1) client_ms, s.service_name ssvc, s.attr_k8s_pod_name spod, round(s.duration/1e6,2) server_ms, round((s.time - c.time)/1e3) start_offset_us, round((c.time + c.duration::BIGINT*interval 1 nanosecond - s.time - s.duration::BIGINT*interval 1 nanosecond)/1e6,1) x FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.trace_id = c.trace_id WHERE c.span_name LIKE 'rate.Rate%' ORDER BY client_ms DESC LIMIT 15

SELECT c.trace_id, c.attr_k8s_pod_name cpod, round(c.duration/1e6,1) client_ms, s.attr_k8s_pod_name spod, round(s.duration/1e6,2) server_ms, round(epoch(s.time)-epoch(c.time),4) start_offset_s FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.trace_id = c.trace_id WHERE c.span_name LIKE 'rate.Rate%' ORDER BY client_ms DESC

input.query: SELECT c.attr_k8s_pod_name cpod, s.attr_k8s_pod_name spod, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) client_ms, round(min(c.duration)/1e6,1) cmin, round(max(c.duration)/1e6,1) cmax, round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,2) server_ms, round(avg(epoch(s.time)-epoch(c.time)),4) avg_start_off_s FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.trace_id = c.trace_id WHERE c.span_name LIKE 'rate.Rate%' GROUP BY 1,2

content.text: The extra time is entirely before the request reaches `rate`: the server span starts about one client-duration after the client span, and the rate server work itself stays around 0.3 ms. Next I'll read the four log rows (the earlier query failed on a timestamp column) and map the full call graph to see which other callers reach `rate`.

input.query: SELECT service_name, level, message, attr_k8s_pod_name, attr_log_template FROM abnormal_logs

SELECT DISTINCT c.service_name caller, c.span_name, s.service_name callee, s.span_name callee_span FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.trace_id = c.trace_id WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client'

content.text: The call graph is clear: `search` is the only caller of `rate`, and its `GetRates` calls carry the delay. I'll check the shape of that delay distribution to help tell a per-request HTTP hold from a link-level delay.

input.query: SELECT CASE WHEN p='ab' THEN 'abnormal' ELSE 'normal' END period, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.1)/1e6,2) p10, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.25)/1e6,2) p25, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,2) p50, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.75)/1e6,2) p75, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,2) p90, round(max(duration)/1e6,1) mx FROM (SELECT 'ab' p, * FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'n', * FROM normal_traces) WHERE service_name='search' AND span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' GROUP BY 1

content.text: The delay is tight (about 1.4–1.6 s, p10 to p90) against a normal p50 of 0.9 ms, which looks like a fixed added delay. To separate a link-level delay from a caller-side HTTP hold, I'll check pod network I/O on search and rate.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, round(avg(CASE WHEN p='ab' THEN value END),1) ab_avg, round(avg(CASE WHEN p='n' THEN value END),1) n_avg FROM (SELECT 'ab' p, * FROM abnormal_metrics_sum UNION ALL SELECT 'n', * FROM normal_metrics_sum) WHERE metric = 'k8s.pod.network.io' AND service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','geo') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2

content.text: I've gathered enough to answer. Recording the reasoning before writing the final output.

input.reflection: Findings: Only the /hotels path (frontend -> search.Search/Nearby -> rate.Rate/GetRates) degrades; ~1.6s extra. Rate's own server span stays ~0.5ms, so the extra time sits in search's client call before rate receives it. No restarts, uptime resets, CPU/memory saturation, or network errors. Pod network io unchanged. search->geo calls are unaffected, so the effect is scoped to one outgoing path (GetRates). No hubble per-connection metrics exist. Best fit: http_slow at the calling service search (held back at the HTTP layer, connection healthy). Propagation: search -> frontend. Other small shifts (profile/reservation memcached, ~0.1-0.4ms) are minor and not user-visible.
